issues.title: Logger uses direct logging.getLogger initialization
issues.description: The rule requires logger instances to be created using the pattern `logger: "logging.Logger" = get_logger("module_name")` from prefect.logging, but the code uses the direct `logging.getLogger(__name__)` pattern instead.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# Logger for SDK fetcher operations
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
issues.rule_name: Logger Instances Must Follow Standard Initialization Pattern

issues.title: Incorrect deployment filtering breaks full-name matching
issues.description: The deployment filtering logic checks `dep.name not in deployment_names` instead of checking `full_name not in deployment_names`. This causes the filter to incorrectly evaluate when users specify deployment names in 'flow-name/deployment-name' format. When a user provides a full deployment name like 'my-flow/production', the code checks if 'production' (the short name) is in the list containing 'my-flow/production', which fails, causing the deployment to enter the fallback matching logic unnecessarily. This breaks the fast-path check and could lead to incorrect filtering behavior where deployments are included or excluded inappropriately.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# If filtering by deployment name, check the full name matches
        full_name = f"{flow_name}/{dep.name}"
        if deployment_names and dep.name not in deployment_names:
            # Only include if the full name matches (filter was by name parts)
            # Skip if user specified full names and this doesn't match
            found_match = False

issues.title: Missing type validation for work pool job variables schema
issues.description: The code removes the `isinstance(variables, dict)` type check before assigning `base_job_template["variables"]` to `job_vars_schema`. The `job_vars_schema` variable is typed as `dict[str, Any]` and is expected to be a dictionary throughout the SDK generation process. If `base_job_template["variables"]` contains a non-dict value (like a list, string, or other type due to malformed work pool configuration), this will cause type inconsistencies that could lead to runtime errors in downstream code that expects a dict, such as the template renderer or SDK generator that processes the schema.

issues.title: Removed strict zip validation enables silent data corruption
issues.description: The code removes `strict=True` from the `zip(pool_names_list, results)` call in the work pool parallel fetching logic. The strict parameter ensures that both iterables have the same length and raises a ValueError if they don't match. Without it, if there's a mismatch between the number of work pool names and the results from `asyncio.gather()` (which should never happen in correct code but could occur due to bugs in the async gather logic or unexpected exceptions), the zip will silently truncate to the shorter sequence. This means some work pool results could be dropped or mismatched with the wrong names, leading to incorrect work pool metadata in the generated SDK without any warning or error.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20241 - Add documentation for prefect sdk generate CLI

structured_output.summary:
The PR is described as docs-only. It adds a how-to guide for `prefect sdk generate`, an auto-generated CLI reference page, and updates navigation in docs.json. It also changes `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`, which the description doesn't mention. Those code edits make the SDK fetcher worse in three ways:
- The deployment-name filter now checks `dep.name` instead of `full_name`, so the warning for an ambiguous short name never fires and the existing test for it fails.
- A type guard on work pool `variables` was removed, so a malformed template can crash code generation.
- `strict=True` was dropped from a `zip`.

A logger was also added in the middle of the import block.

The new guide's async example is wrong too. `PrefectFlowRunFuture.result()` is synchronous, so `await future.result()` will raise.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The unexplained fetcher changes undo existing safeguards. The deployment-filter edit breaks the ambiguous-short-name warning, which `test_fetch_sdk_data_ambiguous_short_name_warning` checks. The async doc example also tells users to write code that fails. The fetcher should be reverted and the doc fixed before merge.

architecture.overview:
`prefect sdk generate` (src/prefect/cli/sdk.py) calls the SDK generator. The generator uses `fetch_sdk_data` in src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py to:
- read deployments, using server-side filters on flow and deployment name
- look up flow names
- fetch work pools in parallel
- filter the results again on the client to exact `flow/deployment` names, warning when a short deployment name matches deployments in more than one flow.

The renderer then uses each work pool's `job_variables_schema` and the deployments' parameter schemas to build the typed SDK from a Jinja template.

The PR mainly adds docs: a how-to page, a CLI reference page, and navigation changes. It also edits the fetcher. It changes the client-side name check from full names to short names, removes the dict type guard on work pool `variables`, drops `strict=True` from a `zip`, and adds a debug logger.
steps: Start at docs/docs.json: a new 'Deployments' nav group holds form-building and the new generate-custom-sdk page, and the CLI reference list gains `sdk`.
Read docs/v3/advanced/generate-custom-sdk.mdx and compare the examples against src/prefect/_sdk/templates/sdk.py.jinja (with_options, with_infra, run, run_async).
In src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py, `fetch_sdk_data` builds server-side filters from the short deployment names, then re-filters on the client using `full_name` (around line 397).
`_fetch_work_pool` pulls `base_job_template['variables']` into `WorkPoolInfo.job_variables_schema`, which `renderer.py` uses by calling `.get('properties')`.
`_fetch_work_pools_parallel` pairs each pool name with its gather result using `zip`.

findings.title: Deployment filter now checks the short name, so the ambiguous-name warning never fires
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`, around line 397 inside `fetch_sdk_data`, the client-side deployment filter was changed to `if deployment_names and dep.name not in deployment_names:`. When a short name is given, this skips the block that fills `short_name_matches`, so the ambiguous-short-name warning is never emitted. Change it back to `if deployment_names and full_name not in deployment_names:`. Then run `tests/_sdk/test_fetcher.py::TestFetchSDKData::test_fetch_sdk_data_ambiguous_short_name_warning` and confirm it passes.

findings.title: Removing the dict guard on `variables` can crash rendering
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` `_fetch_work_pool` (around lines 178-182), restore the `isinstance(variables, dict)` check before assigning `base_job_template['variables']` to `job_vars_schema`. Otherwise a non-dict value reaches `renderer.py` line ~271, where `schema.get('properties')` raises AttributeError. Consider adding a test in `tests/_sdk/test_fetcher.py` where `variables` is a list, and assert that `job_variables_schema == {}`.

findings.title: Async doc example awaits the synchronous `future.result()`
findings.fixPrompt: In `docs/v3/advanced/generate-custom-sdk.mdx`, line 132 of the 'Async usage' example uses `await future.result()`. `PrefectFlowRunFuture.result()` is synchronous (see `src/prefect/futures.py` around line 410), so this raises TypeError. Change it to `await future.aresult()`. Check the rest of the page for any other await on sync methods.

findings.title: `strict=True` dropped from the zip of pool names and gather results
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` line 220 (`_fetch_work_pools_parallel`), restore `strict=True` on `zip(pool_names_list, results)` so a length mismatch raises instead of silently truncating.

findings.title: Logger defined in the middle of the import block
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` lines 19-20, move the `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` definition and its comment below all imports, after the `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block, so there are no E402 violations. Keep `import logging` with the other stdlib imports.

findings.title: Guide's API examples match the generated template
findings.body: I checked the documented `with_options()` keywords (`tags`, `idempotency_key`, `work_queue_name`, `as_subflow`, `scheduled_time`, `flow_run_name`) and the `with_infra()`, `run()`, `run_async()` and `from_name()` methods against `src/prefect/_sdk/templates/sdk.py.jinja`. They all match, apart from the async `result()` problem above. The CLI reference page also matches the help text in `src/prefect/cli/sdk.py`.
